region: Capriva del Friuli · Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Italy
about: Roncús is the small estate of Marco Perco in Capriva del Friuli, a village on the edge of the Collio hills near the Slovenian border. Italian writers call him a ‘philosopher winegrower’, and he is regarded as one of the country’s finest white-wine makers. He farms about ten hectares in small plots, the ‘ronchi’ of the local dialect, from the Latin for clearing, some planted with vines around seventy years old, and makes fewer than 50,000 bottles a year.

Friulano is the region’s signature native white grape, long known as Tocai Friulano. Perco’s comes from vineyards around Cormons, on the gravelly plain of the Isonzo DOC. He uses no herbicides or synthetic fertilisers, ferments with native yeasts only, and lets the wine rest on its lees for about eighteen months in stainless steel before bottling it unfiltered. Like all his whites, it is released late, so it reaches the table with more depth than a young, fresh Friulano.

Friulano typically shows ripe pear and yellow stone fruit with subtle floral notes and a faint bitter-almond finish. Perco’s whites are noted for their minerality, saline edge and persistence, and they are made to evolve in bottle for years. At ten years old, this 2016 has moved past its first freshness toward the mature, gently nutty character, a rare chance to taste an older Friulano.
